primary_claim: In Gemma 2 2B IT, subtracting a difference-in-means 'jailbreak direction' from residual-stream activations (activation addition) drops the jailbreak attack success rate from about 60% to 0% on a held-out test set including unseen jailbreak communities, while directional ablation of the same direction instead makes the model much more vulnerable (ASR rising to 85-97%); both interventions increase refusal on harmless prompts from 3.15% to about 18.88%.

effect.metric: jailbreak attack success rate (ASR, via Llama Guard 2 / HarmBench)

contradicts_or_qualifies: directional ablation, unlike the activation-addition intervention and unlike the related direction-based approach of Ball et al. (arXiv:2406.09289), made the model much more vulnerable to jailbreaks rather than less -- an unexplained result
stated_future_work: Study whether the findings of this project generalize to other datasets and models
Explore ways to reduce the tension between helpfulness and harmfulness (scaling the vector, using bigger models, and/or a smaller training set)
Use this approach to prevent other types of model misbehavior, such as sycophancy or deception
Evaluate if the effects of applying this approach can be fine-tuned away
limitations_stated: further research is needed to assess whether these findings generalize to novel jailbreaks
both interventions came at the cost of reducing helpfulness by making the model refuse some harmless prompts
It is not yet understood why [directional ablation made the model much more vulnerable]
if a jailbreak is successful even after applying this method, this approach will not make the model's output less harmful
quote: the attack success rate dropped from 60% to 0%. Additionally, that indicates that a direction representing jailbreaks might exist and disabling it could make all jailbreaks unsuccessful.
